text: Following them at a short distance. <break time="0.8s" /> Came two elderly women. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the lower middle class. <break time="0.8s" /> One stout and ponderous. <break time="0.8s" /> The other rosy cheeked and nimble. <break time="0.8s" /> Who were watching the old mans strange behavior. <break time="0.8s" /> With great curiosity. <break time="0.8s" /> Like most people of their station. <break time="0.8s" /> They were fascinated by any sign of an odd mind. <break time="0.8s" /> But they were too far off. <break time="0.8s" /> To be certain. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether his gestures were merely eccentric or genuinely mad. <break time="0.8s" /> After they had scrutinized the old mans back. <break time="0.8s" /> In silence for a moment. <break time="0.8s" /> And given each other a queer, sly look. <break time="0.8s" /> They went on energetically. <break time="0.8s" /> Piecing together their very complicated dialogue. <break time="0.8s" /> Nell, Bert, Lot, Cess, Phil, Pa. <break time="0.8s" /> He says, I says, she says. <break time="0.8s" /> I says, I says, I says, said one. <break time="0.8s" /> And the other answered. <break time="0.8s" /> With a list of her own. <break time="0.8s" /> My Bert, Sis, Bill, Grandad, the old man, sugar. <break time="0.8s" /> The ponderous woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Looked through the pattern of falling words. <break time="0.8s" /> At the flowers standing cool, firm, and upright in the earth. <break time="0.8s" /> With a curious expression on her face. <break time="0.8s" /> She saw them. <break time="0.8s" /> As a sleeper waking from a heavy sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> Sees a brass candlestick. <break time="0.8s" /> Reflecting the light in an unfamiliar way. <break time="0.8s" /> And she gazed at them. <break time="0.8s" /> Wide awake. <break time="0.8s" /> With all her powers. <break time="0.8s" /> The heavy woman came to a standstill. <break time="0.8s" /> Opposite the flower bed. <break time="0.8s" /> And ceased even to pretend to listen. <break time="0.8s" /> Letting the words fall over her. <break time="0.8s" /> Until she suggested. <break time="0.8s" /> That they should find a seat. <break time="0.8s" /> And have their tea. <break time="0.8s" /> Meanwhile the snail had considered every possible method. <break time="0.8s" /> Of reaching its goal. <break time="0.8s" /> Without going round the dead leaf or climbing over it. <break time="0.8s" /> And it had finally decided to creep beneath it.
